title: The Pragmatic Programmer
author: Andrew Hunt & David Thomas
summary: A classic guide for software developers that emphasizes practical approaches, adaptability, and continuous learning to write maintainable code.

title: Clean Code
author: Robert C. Martin
summary: Presents principles and patterns for writing readable, testable, and maintainable code, with case studies and heuristics for refactoring.

title: Design Patterns
author: Erich Gamma et al.
summary: Introduces reusable object-oriented design patterns that solve common software engineering problems and improve system flexibility.

title: Domain-Driven Design
author: Eric Evans
summary: Explores how to align complex software design with business domains through ubiquitous language, bounded contexts, and rich domain models.

title: Refactoring
author: Martin Fowler
summary: A catalog of techniques for improving the design of existing code while preserving behavior, making it easier to understand and extend.

title: You Don't Know JS
author: Kyle Simpson
summary: A deep dive into JavaScript's core mechanisms, including scope, closures, this, prototypes, and asynchronous programming.

title: The Mythical Man-Month
author: Frederick P. Brooks Jr.
summary: Brooks' essays on software project management, including the famous observation that adding manpower to a late project makes it later.

title: Introduction to Algorithms
author: Thomas H. Cormen et al.
summary: A comprehensive reference covering a wide range of algorithms and data structures, with analysis and design techniques.

title: Continuous Delivery
author: Jez Humble & David Farley
summary: Describes practices for building, testing, and deploying software reliably and rapidly through automation and fast feedback loops.

title: Building Microservices
author: Sam Newman
summary: Offers practical guidance on designing, building, and operating microservice-based systems, including trade-offs and integration patterns.

title: Site Reliability Engineering
author: Niall Richard Murphy et al.
summary: Explains how Google runs production systems, blending software engineering with operations to create scalable and reliable services.

title: The Phoenix Project
author: Gene Kim et al.
summary: A business novel that illustrates DevOps principles through the story of an IT organization turning around a failing project and company.
